title: Clothes
subtitle: hem, cuff, baggy, it suits you
summary: Name the parts of your clothes, describe their fit, style and pattern, and use suit, match and fit correctly.

lesson.heading: Parts of clothes and shoes
rows: the part that goes round the neck of a shirt or coat
the end of a sleeve, at the wrist
the part that covers your arm
the folded and sewn bottom edge of a skirt or dress
the fastener with two rows of small teeth
the small round fastener you push through a hole
the strip round your waist / the metal fastener on it
the part of a coat or top that covers your head
a small piece of cloth or metal with a design on it
the small tag inside a garment with the size and washing instructions
the bottom of a shoe / the raised part under the back of a shoe
the strings you tie to fasten your shoes

lesson.heading: Some items of clothing
rows: a casual top with a hood
a knitted jacket that buttons up the front
the loose top and trousers you sleep in
a hard hat that protects your head, e.g. on a motorbike

lesson.heading: Clothes that are always plural
lesson.text: Most items of clothing that cover the legs are plural words only. To count them you need **a pair of**.

examples.text: six **pairs of** trousers / shorts / tights / jeans / underpants
Jamie's football shorts **are** too small for him now. I need to get him a new **pair**.
I've got a hole in my tights. I'll have to change into a new **pair**.

lesson.heading: Verbs associated with clothing
lesson.text: Notice the little phrasal verbs used for altering clothes: you **let out** or **take in** for width, and **let down** or **take up** for length.

examples.text: Can I **try on** these grey shoes in the window?
I love **dressing up** for parties as I normally wear jeans.
The skirt is too tight and too short - it needs **letting out** and **letting down**.
The dress is too loose and too long - it needs **taking in** and **taking up**.
He **changed out of** his weekend clothes **into** his uniform.
Those shoes don't fit my son any more. He's **grown out of** them.

lesson.heading: suit, match or fit?
rows: Red usually doesn't **suit** people with ginger hair.
These shoes don't **fit** my son any more.

lesson.heading: Describing clothes
rows: denim (jeans are usually made of this), woollen (made of wool), suede (a kind of leather that isn't shiny)
plain, striped, pinstriped, checked, spotted, flowery, tartan

lesson.heading: Other useful expressions
lesson.text: A few more phrases that come up whenever people talk about what they wear.

examples.text: Anna always looks very elegant even when she's **dressed casually**.
examples.note: casually = in a casual or informal way

examples.text: I don't think it's worth spending money on **designer** sunglasses.
examples.note: designer = made by a famous or fashionable designer

examples.text: Does your country have a special **national costume**?
Alessandra's put her top on **inside out** - I can see the label!
The burglars wore **masks** and hoods as a **disguise** so that no one would recognise them.

lesson.text: *It suits you* is about the person; *it fits you* is about the size; *it matches* is about another garment. Mixing them up is one of the commonest clothes mistakes.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the part of a garment or shoe it names.

pairs.right: the part that goes round your neck
the end of a sleeve, at the wrist
the sewn bottom edge of a skirt
the metal fastener on a belt
the tag inside showing the size

exercises.prompt: I must get my black shoes repaired. One ___ is broken and both the soles have holes in them.
exercises.explanation: The heel is the raised part under the back of a shoe.

exercises.prompt: Do up your ___ or you'll fall over.
exercises.explanation: You do up (or tie) your laces.

exercises.prompt: I've almost finished making my dress but I've still got to take up the ___ and sew on some buttons.
exercises.explanation: To take up a hem is to shorten a garment.

exercises.prompt: You must wear a ___ when you ride a motorbike.
Maya packed her beach towel but forgot her ___, so she couldn't go swimming.
exercises.explanation: A bikini is a two-piece swimming costume.

exercises.prompt: Dad needs some new underpants. Can you buy him three ___ today?
exercises.explanation: Clothes that cover the legs are plural only, so you count them in pairs.

exercises.prompt: The blue of her dress ___ the blue of her eyes.
exercises.explanation: *Match* is used when one thing goes well with another.

exercises.prompt: That blue dress really ___ the girl with the blonde hair.
exercises.explanation: *Suit* is used when something looks good on a person.

exercises.prompt: Is each word a material or a pattern?

exercises.statement: Alessandra has put her top on inside out - that is why you can see the label.
exercises.explanation: Correct - inside out means the inside of the garment is now on the outside.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to explain why the shoes are going to the charity shop.
exercises.answer: Those shoes don't fit him any more. He's grown out of them.
exercises.explanation: *Fit* is about size; to *grow out of* clothes is to become too big for them.
